rootCause: renderWithGradientBg uses theme.background.colors[0] which is NULL when Pexels render fails. Falls back to default color #0a0a1a (almost black). Combined with vignette filter, output is completely black.

renderFlow.step3: hexToRgb(null.background.colors[0]) throws error or returns undefined
renderFlow.step3_fallback: DEFAULT to #0a0a1a (hex code 10,10,26 RGB = very dark almost black)
renderFlow.step4: FFmpeg: color=c=#0a0a1a + vignette filter = completely black output

problematicCode.issue: If theme is null/undefined, hexToRgb gets called with null.background which throws. Then default #0a0a1a is used - a dark color.

assetStatus.conclusion: All Pexels assets are valid and accessible. Problem is NOT missing assets.

ffmpegCommand.issue: color input is #0a0a1a (almost black) due to missing theme
ffmpegCommand.filter_complex_issue: No problem with filter itself. Problem is INPUT (color=black)

whyRenderWithPexelsFailed.comment: Code rejects multi-segment renders due to Windows 32KB command line limit

fixes.fix1: Ensure theme is ALWAYS passed to renderWithGradientBg, never null
fixes.fix2: If theme is null, use DEFAULT BRIGHT color (e.g., #1a1a2e or a vibrant color), NOT #0a0a1a
fixes.fix4: Throw error instead of silently using dark default if theme missing
fixes.fix5: ALTERNATIVELY: Don't fall back to gradient at all. Use split-screen render or reject the video with error.

renderErrorReason: Missing theme data when falling back from failed Pexels render
recommendations: Check why theme is not being passed to script.json generation
Ensure renderWithGradientBg always receives a valid theme with background.colors[0]
Change default color from #0a0a1a to #1a3a4a (visible blue-gray) instead of almost-black
Add error logging: log the theme object before trying to access colors[0]
Add validation: if (!theme || !theme.background || !theme.background.colors[0]) throw clear error
Consider: should we fall back to split-screen instead of gradient if Pexels fails?
